text: We often discuss calendar overload as a productivity drain, but we rarely address it as an accessibility blind spot. When we schedule back-to-back meetings without buffers, we inadvertently exclude neurodivergent colleagues and those with chronic conditions who require transition time. For many, a five-minute gap isn't just a breather; it is a vital necessity to decompress, manage sensory input, or physically reset. To build truly inclusive environments, we must stop viewing empty space as wasted time and start respecting it as a fundamental requirement for participation.
